items.title: Quebec author accused of using AI admits past plagiarism but maintains novel is his own work
items.excerpt: Thélyson Orélien, whose novel was dropped from the Goncourt selection after a Pangram AI-detector flagged it, publicly denies using AI to write it while admitting to plagiarism in earlier columns — a new turn in the AI-detection-vs-author dispute.

history_match.title: Canadian author Thélyson Orélien accused of using AI to write award-winning novel

items.title: How much AI is in Spain's bestselling books?
items.excerpt: EL PAÍS ran 175 popular titles through the Pangram detector: no trace of AI in 2019, but now one in three self-published bestsellers is written mostly with AI, including a top-charting book by politician Alvise Pérez.

items.title: AI companies' book hunt sparks copyright concerns in Türkiye's publishing industry
items.excerpt: Turkish publishers warn that AI companies buying and scanning printed books without permission threatens copyright, while some see a potential new licensing revenue stream.

items.title: Publishers urged to join appeal for greater AI transparency
items.excerpt: More than 150 publishers and organizations back the Frankfurt Appeal from the German Publishers and Booksellers Association, demanding that the EU and Germany require AI developers to disclose the works used to train their models.

items.title: Opening of the 2026 Frankfurt Book Fair: Czech culture minister booed, solidarity with Ukraine, and AI copyright concerns
items.excerpt: The grand opening ceremony of the 2026 Frankfurt Book Fair was held on Oct. 6 at the Congress Center Messe Frankfurt, with Czechia as this year’s guest of honor.

items.title: Book Distributor Giant Nippan Sells Books to U.S. AI Developer Anthropic, Japan Book Publishers Association Requests Stoppage
items.excerpt: A Nippan subsidiary sold Japanese books to Anthropic between Dec 2024 and Dec 2025 without notifying publishers, likely for its book-scanning AI training project; the Japan Book Publishers Association has demanded the sales stop.

history_match.title: Authors Guild Calls on Publishers to Share Anthropic Wealth

items.title: An editor's first read must not be outsourced to AI
items.excerpt: Copy editor Adnan Algın argues that using AI too early in the editorial process can suppress an editor's vital but indefinable first-read instincts on a manuscript.

items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: English language exports, AI and travel chaos lead conversations
items.excerpt: English-language exports, the industry-wide impact of AI, missed meetings caused by “travel chaos” and hall configuration were all hotly debated at this year’s Frankfurt Book Fair.

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: Audible-Commissioned Survey Finds Audio Sends Readers Back to Print; Half Would Try AI Narration
items.excerpt: An Audible-commissioned NielsenIQ survey across 11 markets finds audiobooks pull listeners toward print and e-books, and that about half of listeners would be open to AI-narrated titles.

items.title: Publishers Hit the AI Jackpot
items.excerpt: Publishers stand to gain the most from Anthropic's $1.5 billion copyright settlement over pirated books — and many writers aren't happy about how the money is being split.

history_match.title: Authors Guild Calls on Publishers to Share Anthropic Wealth

items.title: Google launched Expert Intelligence on Google Play Books
items.excerpt: Google's Expert Intelligence is now live in Play Books with 100,000+ licensed titles; a Gemini/NotebookLM integration lets readers generate quizzes, infographics and Audio Overviews from books combined with their own notes.

history_match.title: Google launches Expert Intelligence with more than 100k publisher titles

items.title: How to Listen to Kindle Books With CastReader
items.excerpt: A hands-on guide to CastReader, which reads Kindle books aloud with cloud AI voices and offers an 'AI Explain' feature for unfamiliar passages, via the phone app or Kindle Cloud Reader.

items.title: S&S Re-Ups with H.M. Wolfe in Seven-Figure Deal
items.excerpt: Simon & Schuster signs a seven-figure romantasy duology deal with H.M. Wolfe, months after The Atlantic cited a Pangram detector reading of 60% AI to claim her hit Daggermouth was AI-assisted.

items.title: New detector spots AI-generated work by examining ideas, not words
items.excerpt: IdeaLens, from UMD, Google DeepMind and Simon Fraser researchers, flags AI writing by analyzing underlying ideas rather than style, catching 91% of fully AI-written documents with 0.6% false alarms — but it is uneven on mixed human-AI texts.
